metadata.name: DentFlow AI - Voice Receptionist for Dental Clinics

idea: AI Voice Receptionist for Dental Practices that handles 24/7 inbound emergency calls, insurance pre-checks, and syncs appointments with Dentrix and Open Dental EHRs.

competitors.name: Syllable
weaknesses: Aimed at hospitals, not SMB clinics

trends: Dental front-desk staff turnover exceeds 38% annually
Rising patient expectation for 24/7 instant appointment bookings
Voice AI latency dropping below 500ms enabling natural conversation
risks: HIPAA compliance liability for voice recordings and patient health information
EHR write-back conflicts when front desk double-books slots manually
Handling dental emergencies with strict liability disclaimers

prd.problem_statement: Private dental clinics lose an estimated $75,000 annually per chair due to missed after-hours calls, unanswered emergency booking inquiries, and front-desk phone congestion during peak morning hours.

personas.name: Dr. Sarah Lin
pain_points: Misses high-value implant consultations after 5 PM

personas.name: Mark Ramirez
pain_points: Spends 3 hours daily on routine insurance verification phone calls
goals: Automate insurance pre-checks before patients arrive

features.name: Autonomous Inbound Voice Dispatcher
features.description: Sub-600ms latency telephony voice bot handling scheduling, rescheduling, and FAQ.

features.name: Dentrix / Open Dental 2-Way Sync
features.description: Direct calendar write-back preventing double bookings.

features.name: Emergency Triage Routing
features.description: Detects dental trauma/severe pain and forwards to on-call dentist cell.

features.name: Insurance Eligibility Lookup
features.description: Pings clearinghouse APIs to verify copay and coverage eligibility.

prd.mvp_scope: Deliver single-location clinic support with Dentrix local sync bridge within 8 weeks using 2 full-stack developers.
user_stories: As a patient with a chipped tooth at 9 PM, I want to book a morning slot via phone so I get emergency care.
As a practice manager, I want calls logged in our EHR so staff don't have to take manual notes.
As a practice owner, I want HIPAA-compliant audio encryption so our clinic avoids regulatory fines.

stack.justification: Async ASGI engine for low-latency WebSocket telephony streaming
Ultra low latency audio pipelines with sub-200ms frame transmission
Serverless transactional storage with encrypted health record columns
Stateful phone call session cache and slot locking mechanism
Industry-leading accuracy for medical dental terminology

architecture.diagram_mermaid:
graph TD
  Patient((Patient Call)) --> Twilio[Twilio Voice SIP]
  Twilio --> LiveKit[LiveKit WebRTC Server]
  LiveKit --> Engine[FastAPI Voice Engine]
  Engine --> STT[Deepgram Nova-2]
  Engine --> LLM[Claude 3.5 Sonnet]
  Engine --> TTS[Cartesia Sonic]
  Engine --> SyncBridge[Dentrix Sync Bridge]
  SyncBridge --> ClinicEHR[(Clinic Dentrix DB)]
risks: EHR API local socket disconnections on Windows Server practice computers
Network jitter on clinic Wi-Fi causing voice dropouts
Dialect variations in dental terminology misrecognized by STT
